title: agentseam vendor config entry
description: docs/design/dialect-families.md §3: config may carry strings, booleans, ordered lists
of strings, and flat maps of those -- nothing else. The single deliberate exception is
`evidence`, a map of claim-id to a flat {basis, date, test} record (owner decision
2026-09-01, org-plan plan/agentseam-project.md: every claim in a vendor entry carries
its own basis/date/test-id, and schema validation fails a claim with none). Unknown
keys are an error everywhere in this schema on purpose (§5 'Must be written' item 1):
a typo'd key must fail loud, not fail open.

events.description: vendor wire event name -> canonical event. Empty only for antigravity, whose payloads carry no event name at all (dialect-families.md §1).

wire_events.description: canonical event -> vendor wire name, present ONLY where it differs from the naive inverse of `events` (a many-to-one vendor vocabulary collapsed, with the emit direction pinned deliberately).

fields.description: canonical Event field -> ordered fallback chain of dotted vendor keys tried in `parse()`.

fields_memory_write.description: vscode_copilot only: the field chains that apply instead of `fields` when the tool call is a memory-tool write (vscode_copilot.py:66-73).

answer_events.description: vendor wire event names at which this dialect ever speaks a verdict word (a subset of the keys of `gates`).

gates.description: vendor wire event name -> what that gate honours. Keys are vendor names, not canonical ones, because one canonical event can carry several wire names with different honours_escalate (cursor.py:51-57). Field names follow the post-W35 ACS vocabulary (contract.py: escalate/transform), not the pre-ACS ask/rewrite.

words.description: decision concept -> the word this dialect speaks for it (dialect-families.md §3.2). A missing key means the concept is never spoken (a bare allow stays silent, a vouch degrades to silence).

degrade_notes.description: the degradation-note strings, verbatim from the adapter they replaced so wire output stays byte-identical (dialect-families.md §3.1). `*_gate` keys apply at G2 gates; `escalate_from_transform` wins when the escalate was degraded from a transform.

reason_defaults.description: reason text spoken when the handler gave none, per refusal kind; the engine falls back to "blocked by policy".

note_style.description: suffix: default the reason first, then always append " (note)"; because: "reason (note)" only when both exist, then default an empty result.

echo.description: where a hookSpecificOutput body's hookEventName comes from: the payload's own event name, or this entry's canonical->wire mapping.

default_wire_event.description: wire event name respond() assumes when the payload carries none (devin's PreToolUse).

context_events.description: vendor wire event names where additionalContext is spoken.

context_source.description: which Decision field feeds additionalContext at context_events.

matcher.description: whether passing `matcher=` to hook_config() changes its output at all.

bare.description: the hooks table IS the whole config value, with no wrapper key around it (devin's hooks.v1.json).

group.description: top-level wrapper key when the hooks table sits inside one (antigravity's GROUP).

entry_extra.description: flat map of the vendor-specific extra fields this adapter's hook_config() entries carry (commandWindows, name, windows, or windsurf's extra pre_mcp_tool_use wiring), verbatim.

evidence.description: per-claim evidence (owner decision 2026-09-01). One entry per claim-id in $defs/claimIds; schema validation fails a claim with none.

keyChain.description: ordered, first-present-wins; dotted (`tool_input.file_path`) for a nested key, `name[].key` for a fallback that joins a list.

client_types.description: accepted values of the vendor's own client-type field; null means the field may be absent.

accept_names.description: vendor event names accepted unconditionally, before any other check -- names no other vendor sends (devin's PermissionRequest/PostCompaction).

accept_when_all.description: vendor event name -> keys that must ALL be present for that event to be claimed when no accept_marker is (codex_cli's SessionStart compound check).

reject_markers_unless_probe.description: probe name -> markers that reject the payload UNLESS the named probe passes it (claude_code's prompt_id, rescued by looks_like_claude_code).

reject_probes.description: named engine predicates (e.g. looks_like_claude_code) -- the design's own [h]: config may cite one, never embed its logic (dialect-families.md §7). A payload any listed probe matches is rejected.

notes.description: residual claims() branching this flat marker set does not express; a citation, not a spec.

test.description: golden fixture id or pytest suite node id that exercises this claim against our runtime; null only where none does.
